title: How did home valuation prices perform in Peoria County during Q2?
text:
How did home valuation prices perform in Peoria County during Q2?
The median sale price of a home sold in the second quarter of 2026 in Peoria County rose by $7,800, while total sales increased by 2.7%, according to BlockShopper.com.
From April through June of 2026, 882 homes were sold in the county, with sale prices around averaging $147,800. This is a 5.6% increase over the $140,000 median sale price during the same period in 2025, when there were 859 homes sold.
Based on the latest available data from 2023, the median property tax on homes in Peoria County was $2,798, which equates to 1.9% of the median home sale price for the second quarter of 2026.
U.S. home prices continued to rise in 2025, with the national median reaching about $447,000 in June. That's up 1.13% from a year earlier, according to Redfin. The data also show a significant gap in supply and demand, with 36% more sellers than buyers (a difference of 508,715 homes). By Redfin’s definition, a balanced market has seller and buyer numbers within 10% of each other.
